newsitem.title: GERMANY: German army sacks conscripts for racist attack.
newsitem.headline: German army sacks conscripts for racist attack.

text.p: Two young German army soldiers were discharged with immediate effect on Tuesday for a racist firebombing of a hostel for foreign workers, the latest blow to the image of the country's military.
The Defence Ministry said it was invoking a rule allowing conscripts to be dismissed if their continued presence in the army would constitute a "serious danger to military order".
The conscripts, aged 18 and 20, confessed to setting fire to the building in the eastern city of Dresden on Saturday.
No one was hurt in the blaze. A group of Italian workers who live in the building had gone on holiday a day before the attack, police said.
Authorities found swastikas daubed on the building and witnesses reported that the attackers had shouted Nazi slogans shortly after the fire started.

The incident further sullied the reputation of the German army. A television station last month broadcast pictures of soldiers staging mack executions and rapes during a break in training for a peacekeeping mission in former Yugoslavia.
In March, a group of soldiers went on a rampage attacking foreigners in the western town of Detmold.
Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said the army was not to blame for the behaviour of the two soldiers who carried out the Dresden attack.
The soldiers had been members of society for 20 years but only members of the army for two months, he said.
